boards.title: Eczema drugs
boards.intro: He emphasized crisaborole and the two "-tinib" JAK inhibitors among the eczema drugs (slide 6; T 660–662).

items.name: Crisaborole
items.tell: The shaded ring holds the boron: crisaborole is a benzoxaborole, a boron-bearing soft drug (slide 7; T 683–689, 665–668). In PDE4 the boron binds Zn2+ and Mg2+, its chemical basis of drug action (slide 7; T 712–718).
items.eg: LogP 3 with accumulation in the dermis; t1/2 12 h (slide 7; T 690–697).

items.name: Benzyl alcohol (crisaborole step 1 product)
items.tell: Hydrolytic deboronation in the skin removes the boron without an enzyme and leaves the phenol and the CH2OH shaded here (slide 7; T 699–704, 723–728).

items.name: Benzoic acid (crisaborole step 2 product)
items.tell: The CH2OH becomes the shaded carboxylic acid through two enzymes, alcohol dehydrogenase then aldehyde dehydrogenase (slide 7; T 705–709). Sulfation and glucuronidation (steps 3 and 4) follow (slide 9; T 767–777).

items.name: Ruxolitinib
items.tell: The shaded bicyclic ring is the pyrrolopyrimidine; compare it with upadacitinib's ring: the two are structurally different (slide 8; T 730–733). He said the class names themselves need not be memorized (T 730–732).
items.eg: T1/2 3 h; 3A4/2C9 substrate; some hydroxylated metabolites are active (slide 8; T 745–754).

items.name: Upadacitinib
items.tell: The shaded tricyclic ring is the imidazopyrrolopyridine, a different ring system from ruxolitinib's pyrrolopyrimidine (slide 8; T 730–733).
items.eg: T1/2 8–16 h; 3A4/2D6 substrate; no active metabolites (slide 8; T 745–754).

boards.title: Psoriasis: emollients, anthralin, psoralen
boards.intro: Topical psoriasis agents from the 11/03 lecture (slides 14–18; T 850–977).

items.name: Cyclomethicone
items.tell: A ring of five Si–O units ("a pentamer"): cyclomethicone is the cyclic silicone, dimethicone the linear chain (slide 15; T 885–889). Silicone emollients are hypoallergenic and non-comedogenic (slide 15; T 882–884).

items.name: Anthralin (dithranol)
items.tell: Three fused rings with a central ketone and two OH groups beside it: a hydroxyanthrone (slide 17; T 920). It autoxidizes without enzymes to the anthranyl radical and superoxide anion, its chemical basis of drug action (slide 17; T 928–942).
items.eg: The deck gives logP = 4 (slide 17); he warned not to apply too much because it will go systemic (T 927–928).

items.name: 8-Methoxypsoralen (8-MOP, methoxsalen)
items.tell: Shaded: a furan ring fused to a coumarin, so a furanocoumarin, with the methoxy at C-8 (slide 18; T 958–960). With UVA it covalently binds and crosslinks DNA pyrimidine bases; he said it is the only molecule he would mention with this chemical basis of action (slide 18; T 963–967).
items.eg: Partially inhibits CYP3A4 (slide 18; T 962–963). Unlike anthralin, its action does not involve autoxidation (slide 19; T 977–980).

boards.title: Glucocorticoids
boards.intro: He asked for three things about glucocorticoids: structure, stereochemistry and numbering (slide 20; T 987–990).

items.name: Steroid C-atom numbering skeleton
items.tell: Numbering runs 1 to 10 as a loop around rings A and B, 11 to 17 as a snake over rings C and D, then 18 (methyl on C-13) and 19 (methyl on C-10), then 20 onward on the side chain at C-17 (slide 20; T 1003–1017, 1084–1099).
items.eg: "If you know where your 1 is, you know where your 11 is, and your 17, you're good to go" (T 1098–1099).

items.name: Glucocorticoid SAR: the four features (on fluticasone propionate)
items.tell: Shaded are the four features that increase anti-inflammatory activity: the C1–C2 double bond, 6α-halogen, 9α-halogen and 11β-OH (slide 20; T 1020–1073). Fluticasone propionate (slide 24) carries all four.
items.note: The SAR drawing on slide 20 uses X for the halogens; fluticasone propionate from slide 24 is used here as a molecule that has all four features.

items.name: Hydrocortisone (cortisol)
items.tell: The reference molecule (parent drug) for glucocorticoid activity (slide 24; T 1140–1145). Shaded is the 11β-OH that 11β-HSD oxidizes to cortisone and back: hydrocortisone "ping pongs" between the two (slide 26; T 1190–1196).
items.eg: It binds the glucocorticoid receptor through 6 hydrogen bonds (slide 23; T 1133–1139). LogP about 1.5; t1/2 1–2 h due to metabolism (slide 26; T 1182–1188).
items.note: Slide 25 draws hydrocortisone with HO on C-20 in place of the C-20 ketone; slides 23, 24 and 26 draw the C-20 ketone, which is used here.

items.name: Cortisone
items.tell: Same skeleton as hydrocortisone with a ketone (shaded) at C-11 in place of the 11β-OH; inactive, and formed and reversed by 11β-HSD (slide 26; T 1190–1196; 11/04 T@790).
items.eg: Cortisone and urocortisol are excreted in urine (slide 26).

items.name: 5β-Dihydrocortisol
items.tell: Ring A reduced by 5β-reductase: the C4=C5 double bond is gone and the H at the shaded C-5 is beta; inactive (slide 26).

items.name: Urocortisol
items.tell: 3α-HSD reduces the C-3 ketone of 5β-dihydrocortisol to the shaded 3α-OH; inactive and excreted in urine (slide 26).

items.name: Betamethasone dipropionate
items.tell: Shown in class; he said these derivative structures need not be memorized (T 1152–1154). Shaded: the two propionate esters, at C-17 and C-21; it also has the C1–C2 double bond, 9α-F and 16β-methyl (slide 24).
items.eg: Listed as potent, 0.05% (slide 25).

items.name: Clobetasol propionate
items.tell: Shown in class; he said these derivative structures need not be memorized (T 1152–1154). Compared with hydrocortisone it adds the C1–C2 double bond, 9α-F, 16β-methyl, a 17-propionate and a 21-Cl (shaded); these structural changes, not metabolism, move it from low to high potency (slide 25; T 1175–1179).
items.eg: Listed as super-potent, 0.05% (slide 25).
items.note: Slide 25 draws clobetasol propionate with OH on C-21; slide 24 draws the 21-Cl of the marketed drug, which is used here.

items.name: Desonide
items.tell: Shown in class; he said these derivative structures need not be memorized (T 1152–1154). The shaded ring is a 16α,17α-acetonide (a cyclic acetal with acetone); no fluorine (slide 24).

items.name: Fluticasone propionate
items.tell: Shown in class; he said these derivative structures need not be memorized (T 1152–1154). Shaded: 6α-F and 9α-F, and the 17β carbonyl carries S–CH2F (a thioester) (slide 24).

items.name: Triamcinolone acetonide
items.tell: Shown in class; he said these derivative structures need not be memorized (T 1152–1154). Desonide's 16α,17α-acetonide (shaded) plus a 9α-F (slide 24).

boards.title: Vitamin D
boards.intro: Vitamin D analogs are used in psoriasis for their antiproliferative action; hypercalcemia limits their use (slide 27; 11/04 T@1505–@2000).

items.name: 7-Dehydrocholesterol
items.tell: An intact steroid with the shaded 5,7-diene in ring B; the first step opens ring B, and he said light is involved (slide 27; 11/04 T@2989–@3430, @4330–@4410).
items.eg: The 2-point take-home question asks for the reactions, organs and enzymes of these steps; see the vitamin D3 biosynthesis reading linked on slide 2 (slide 27; 11/04 T@3530–@3660, @4065–@4160).

items.name: Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3)
items.tell: Ring B is open (a secosteroid): the shaded triene with the exocyclic CH2 replaces ring B of 7-dehydrocholesterol (slide 27; 11/04 T@2989–@3430).

items.name: 25-OH-cholecalciferol
items.tell: Cholecalciferol with the shaded OH at C-25 of the side chain; the slide labels it the inactive circulating vitamin D3 (slide 27).

items.name: Calcitriol (1,25-di-OH-cholecalciferol)
items.tell: The active vitamin D3: shaded are the two OH groups added to cholecalciferol, at C-1 (by 1-α-hydroxylase) and C-25 (slide 27). Calcitriol (Rocaltrol) is a secosteroid (slide 27).
items.eg: Both calcitriol and calcipotriene increase calcium absorption, so hypercalcemia limits both (11/04 T@2373–@2830).

items.name: Calcipotriene (Dovonex)
items.tell: Calcitriol's secosteroid core and 1,3-diol with a different side chain: a trans double bond, an OH and the shaded cyclopropyl ring (slide 27). It was an attempt to lower calcium absorption that did not succeed (11/04 T@2373–@2830).
items.note: The deck labels it "Calciprotriene" (slide 27); the drug name is calcipotriene.

boards.title: Limus drugs (calcineurin inhibitors)
boards.intro: Pimecrolimus and tacrolimus are macrolide or lactone immunosuppressants that are similar in lipophilicity, structure and mechanism but differ in skin permeation (slide 28; 11/04 T@4534–@6070).

items.name: Pimecrolimus
items.tell: Shaded are its two differences from tacrolimus: Cl on the cyclohexyl ring (tacrolimus: OH) and an ethyl group (tacrolimus: allyl) (slide 28; 11/04 T@4534–@4700). Higher non-specific skin protein binding keeps it in the skin, so low systemic ADRs (slide 28; 11/04 T@4931–@5300).
items.eg: cLogP 6.0 (slide 28).
items.note: Checked against the Polleve-3 drawing (slide 32), which draws Cl and OCH3 cis as in pimecrolimus. Slide 28 draws the Cl hashed like tacrolimus's OH (trans to OCH3); that differs from the marketed drug, so the slide 32 configuration is used.

items.name: Tacrolimus
items.tell: Shaded are the OH on the cyclohexyl ring and the allyl group, where it differs from pimecrolimus (slide 28; 11/04 T@4534–@4700). Low skin protein binding lets it reach the systemic circulation (slide 28; 11/04 T@5414).
items.eg: cLogP 5.8 (slide 28).

boards.title: Psoriasis: retinoids and systemic agents
boards.intro: Retinoids (slide 29) and the non-biological systemic agents for psoriasis (slides 30–35; 11/04 T@6344–@15120).

items.name: Methotrexate (MTX)
items.tell: The shaded pteridine ring is why it is classed as a pteridine (slide 30; 11/04 T@8238). SAR: pteridine ring, p-aminobenzoic acid and glutamic acid; the pteridine must stay aromatic, alkylating its ring amines lowers activity, and the N-CH3 is essential (slide 31; 11/04 T@10109–@10851).
items.eg: It competitively inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, binding more tightly than folic acid (slide 30; 11/04 T@8545–@9300).
items.note: The slides draw no stereochemistry at the glutamate carbon, so none is given here.

items.name: Folic acid
items.tell: DHFR's substrate, drawn beside methotrexate: shaded are where they differ, OH (MTX: NH2) on the pteridine and N–H (MTX: N–CH3) (slide 31; 11/04 T@8545–@9300).
items.note: Drawn as on the slides, with OH at C-4 of the pteridine.

items.name: Tetrahydrofolic acid
items.tell: Folate reduction by dihydrofolate reductase saturates the shaded ring; the product is an essential cofactor for DNA synthesis (slide 30; 11/04 T@8545–@9300).

items.name: Cyclosporin
items.tell: An 11 amino acid cyclic peptide; its amide bonds in a ring make it a cyclic lactam (slide 33; 11/04 T@12014–@12200). A "prodrug" activated by complexation with cyclophilin, not by metabolism (slide 33; 11/04 T@12289–@12500).
items.eg: PO bioavailability about 30% from first-pass CYP3A4 metabolism; grapefruit juice raises its blood levels (slide 33; 11/04 T@12824–@13690).

items.name: Apremilast (Otezla)
items.tell: The shaded ring system is the isoindoline (slide 34). He stressed its reliance on CYP3A4: O-demethylation to an OH metabolite, then O-glucuronidation (slide 34; 11/04 T@13908–@14319).

items.name: Tofacitinib (Xeljanz)
items.tell: The shaded pyrrolopyrimidine is the same ring as ruxolitinib's; it is a JAK inhibitor like the eczema "-tinibs" (slide 35; 11/04 T@14505–@14700).
items.eg: 70% metabolized by CYP3A4; caution with 3A4 inhibitors and inducers (slide 35; 11/04 T@14700–@15120).

boards.title: Lactone and lactam
boards.intro: He asked how a cyclic drug is classified from a circled functional group: a cyclic ester is a lactone, a cyclic amide a lactam (slide 32; 11/04 T@11280–@11720, @12200).

items.name: Lactone (cyclic ester), in pimecrolimus
items.tell: The shaded ester sits inside the macrocycle, so this limus drug is classed as a lactone; it is not a steroid (slide 32; 11/04 T@11453–@11720).

items.name: Lactam (cyclic amide), in cyclosporin
items.tell: Every shaded amide bond lies in the ring of this cyclic peptide, so it can be described as a cyclic lactam (slide 33; 11/04 T@12014–@12200).

boards.title: Acne: hydroxy acids, sulfur, benzoyl peroxide
boards.intro: Keratolytics break up keratin to promote desquamation; he drew glycolic acid, salicylic acid and benzoyl peroxide (slides 43-47; T@19419).

items.name: Glycolic acid
items.tell: The OH sits on the carbon next to the carboxylic acid, so glycolic acid is an alpha-hydroxy acid; it is hydrophilic (log P about 1, pKa about 3) and acts mostly on the skin surface (slide 43; T@20426, T@20690).
items.eg: The little that reaches the blood is oxidized to a diacid by two enzymes, alcohol dehydrogenase and aldehyde dehydrogenase (slide 43; T@21007).

items.name: Oxalic acid (glycolic acid metabolite)
items.tell: The diacid drawn as the product of glycolic acid after its minimal metabolism by DMEs (slide 43; T@20934).
items.note: The slide draws the product without a name; the course outline names it oxalic acid. He said only "diacid".

items.name: Salicylic acid
items.tell: The OH is on the beta carbon, two carbons from the carboxylic acid, so salicylic acid is a beta-hydroxy acid; the aromatic ring makes it more lipophilic (log P 1-2) than glycolic acid, so it penetrates a little deeper (slide 43; T@22140, T@21540).
items.eg: Of what reaches the systemic circulation, 75% is conjugated with glycine (slide 43; T@22475).

items.name: Tartaric acid
items.tell: Each OH is on a carbon next to a carboxylic acid, so tartaric acid counts as an alpha-hydroxy acid in Polleve-4 (slide 45; T@23518).
items.eg: Also listed as an AHA from grapes on slide 68.

items.name: Isobutyric acid (Polleve-4)
items.tell: A carboxylic acid with no OH group, so it is not a hydroxy acid; one of the five molecules in Polleve-4 (slide 45; T@23385).
items.note: Name supplied for the unlabelled poll drawing.

items.name: Cyclopropyl hydroxy diacid (Polleve-4)
items.tell: The OH is on the carbon next to the right-hand carboxylic acid, so this molecule qualifies as an alpha-hydroxy acid in Polleve-4 (slide 45; T@23801).
items.note: Unnamed on the slide; 1-[carboxy(hydroxy)methyl]cyclopropane-1-carboxylic acid.

items.name: 2-Hydroxycyclohexanecarboxylic acid (Polleve-4)
items.tell: The OH is on the ring carbon two away from the carboxylic acid (beta), so it does not count; by his definition three of the five molecules in Polleve-4 are alpha-hydroxy acids (slide 45; T@23518).
items.note: Unnamed on the slide. He did not speak the final count (T@23865); the definition he gave yields three (tartaric, glycolic, the cyclopropyl diacid).

items.name: Benzoyl peroxide (BPO)
items.tell: The O-O peroxide bond defines its chemical class; the bond breaks to give benzoic acid, which lowers skin pH, and a radical that kills bacteria (slide 47; T@26051).
items.eg: Slide 47 gives log P = 3.5; he said it penetrates skin well (T@25991).

items.name: Benzoic acid
items.tell: One product of the peroxide bond breaking; it lowers skin pH and adds keratolytic activity, and it is excreted in urine (slide 47; T@26109).

items.name: Benzoyl radical
items.tell: The other product of the peroxide bond breaking, an oxygen-centred radical that kills bacteria and accounts for the anti-inflammatory claim (slide 47; T@26270).
items.note: The slide labels it "Benzoyl radical" but draws the benzoyloxy radical PhC(=O)O·, which is what this SMILES gives.

boards.title: Retinoids by generation
boards.intro: All retinoids are vitamin A (retinol) derivatives and RAR/RXR agonists; they are classified by aromatic rings: non-aromatic (1st), mono-aromatic (2nd), poly-aromatic (3rd); all are teratogenic (slides 48-51; T@26805, T@27705).

items.name: Retinol (vitamin A1)
items.tell: The "parent compound": a trimethylcyclohexene ring and an all-trans polyene chain ending in CH2OH; every retinoid in the deck is derived from it (slides 48-49; T@26805).

items.name: Tretinoin
items.tell: All-trans retinoic acid: no aromatic ring and every chain double bond trans; used topically, the first retinoid for acne (slide 49; T@28259).

items.name: Isotretinoin
items.tell: 13-cis retinoic acid: counting from the carboxyl carbon, the C13=C14 double bond is cis and every other one is trans; it is a geometric isomer of tretinoin, used orally (slide 49; T@28448, T@28664).

items.name: Etretinate
items.tell: One aromatic ring (4-methoxy-2,3,6-trimethylphenyl) and an ethyl ester: an ester prodrug that carboxylesterases convert to acitretin; narrow TI, teratogenic, removed from the US market in 1998 (slide 50; T@29146).
items.eg: Slide 50: t1/2 120 days, highly lipophilic.

items.name: Acitretin (Soriatane)
items.tell: The free carboxylic acid of etretinate, the active form used directly; it keeps some teratogenicity, but not to the extent of etretinate (slide 50; T@29322).

items.name: Adapalene (Differin)
items.tell: Three aromatic rings (a methoxyphenyl with an adamantyl group, joined to a naphthoic acid); directly active because of its exposed carboxylic acid; the first synthetic retinoid (slide 51; T@30193).

items.name: Trifarotene (Aklief)
items.tell: Three benzene rings in a row (terphenyl) carrying a pyrrolidine, a tert-butyl and a hydroxyethoxy group; directly active through its exposed carboxylic acid (slide 51; T@30193).

items.name: Tazarotene (Tazorac)
items.tell: A thiochroman and a pyridine joined by an alkyne; the ethyl ester makes it a prodrug that carboxylesterase converts to tazarotenic acid (slide 51; T@30269).
items.eg: Also drawn on slide 70 as a topical retinoid that stimulates collagen production; on slide 29 for psoriasis.
items.note: The structure label on slide 51 reads "Tazarac"; the bullet and slide 70 read Tazorac.

items.name: Tazarotenic acid
items.tell: The active form of tazarotene: the same skeleton with the ester hydrolysed to a free carboxylic acid (slide 51; T@30269).

boards.title: Hormonal agents for acne
boards.intro: Oral contraceptives and antiandrogens both lower sebum production; he contrasted the steroidal and non-steroidal approaches (slides 52-53; T@33093).

items.name: Ethinyl estradiol
items.tell: A steroid (rings A, B, C, D) with an aromatic A ring bearing a phenol and a 17-ethynyl group; co-formulated with norgestimate or drospirenone (slide 52; T@31168).

items.name: Norgestimate
items.tell: A steroid progestin with a 3-oxime, a 17-acetate ester, a 17-ethynyl and a 13-ethyl group; paired with ethinyl estradiol in Ortho Tri-Cyclen Lo (slide 52; T@31076).
items.note: Oxime geometry left unspecified; the slide drawing does not mark it.

items.name: Drospirenone
items.tell: A steroid with two fused cyclopropane rings and a spiro lactone at C17; paired with ethinyl estradiol in Yasmin and Yaz (slide 52; T@31076).

items.name: Spironolactone (Aldactone)
items.tell: The only steroid of the three antiandrogens (four stacked rings plus a spiro lactone and a 7-thioacetate); it decreases testosterone biosynthesis (slide 53; T@32075).

items.name: Ketoconazole
items.tell: Non-steroidal; the imidazole marks it as an azole antifungal, and azoles are strong CYP3A4 inhibitors; here it decreases testosterone biosynthesis (slide 53; T@32479).
items.note: No stereochemistry is drawn on the slide, so none is given here. Slide 53 lists ketoconazole under "Non-steroidal AA"; by mechanism he grouped it with spironolactone (T@32075).

items.name: Flutamide (Eulexin)
items.tell: Non-steroidal: an anilide with nitro and trifluoromethyl groups; it blocks testosterone from binding its receptor (slide 53; T@32753).

boards.title: Antibiotics for acne
boards.intro: P. acnes is gram positive; he asked only that the structures be recognized (linear vs cyclic; tetracyclines vs steroids), the rest is covered in ID (slides 54-55; T@34517).

items.name: Azelaic acid
items.tell: A C9 linear chain with a carboxylic acid at each end (a diacid); a small linear antibiotic that is also anti-inflammatory (slide 54; T@34211).

items.name: Clindamycin
items.tell: A lincomycin: an N-methylpyrrolidine amide linked to a sugar that carries an S-methyl group, with a chlorine on the side chain; used topically because of GI toxicity (slide 54; T@34335).

items.name: Erythromycin
items.tell: A macrolide: a large lactone ring carrying two sugars; a cyclic antibiotic, in contrast to the linear azelaic acid (slide 54; T@34833).
items.eg: Slide 54: poor oral absorption, unstable at pH 4 or lower; acid salts (at the dimethylamino N) and esters (at the sugar OH, both circled) raise water and lipid solubility.

items.name: Tetracycline
items.tell: Four six-membered rings fused in one straight line (rings 1-2-3-4), unlike the stacked steroid rings; C6 carries OH and CH3 (slide 55; T@35220).
items.eg: Slide 55: chelates Al3+, Ca2+, Mg2+, Fe3+, Bi3+ into insoluble salts that stain and weaken bone and enamel; absorption affected by food; t1/2 8.5 h.

items.name: Doxycycline
items.tell: The same linear four-ring skeleton; the OH moves from C6 to C5 and C6 keeps only a methyl; made to overcome the food effect (slide 55; T@36346).
items.eg: Structural similarity means a patient allergic to tetracycline is likely allergic to doxycycline and minocycline (slide 55; T@36772). Slide 55: t1/2 11-13 h.

items.name: Minocycline
items.tell: The same linear four-ring skeleton with a second dimethylamino group on the aromatic ring (C7) and no substituent at C5 or C6; lipophilic and longer acting (slide 55; T@36346).

boards.title: Sunblocks and sunscreens
boards.intro: Inorganic metal oxides reflect or scatter UV; organic sunscreens are chromophores that absorb UV and convert it into harmless heat; he compared them by skin absorption and photodegradation half-life (slides 61-66; T@40042).

items.name: Zinc oxide (ZnO)
items.tell: Not a molecule but a particulate metal oxide that physically reflects or scatters UVA and UVB; larger particles are more effective, nano-sized ZnO turns transparent and loses reflection (slide 61; T@38748).
items.note: Shown as formula ions only; slide 61 has no structure drawing.

items.name: Titanium dioxide (TiO2)
items.tell: A particulate metal oxide reflector like zinc oxide: broad spectrum (UVA and UVB), inert, and more effective as larger particles (slide 61; T@39323).
items.note: Shown as formula ions only; slide 61 has no structure drawing.

items.name: Avobenzone
items.tell: A dibenzoylmethane: two aryl ketones joined by one CH2 (a 1,3-diketone chromophore); low skin absorption, photodegradation t1/2 about 2 h, so reapply every 2 h (slide 62; T@40775).

items.name: Meradimate
items.tell: An anthranilate: a 2-aminobenzoate ester of menthol; absorbs UVA and degrades even more rapidly than avobenzone (slide 62; T@41314).
items.note: No stereochemistry is drawn on the slide, so none is given here.

items.name: Octinoxate
items.tell: A cinnamate: a trans C=C between the methoxyphenyl ring and the ester carbonyl, esterified with 2-ethylhexanol; a UVB absorber that is absorbed through skin, photodegradation t1/2 1-2 h (slide 63; T@41691).

items.name: PABA (p-aminobenzoic acid)
items.tell: An amino group para to a carboxylic acid; rarely used because some people are allergic to PABA (slide 63; T@42015).

items.name: Padimate O
items.tell: A PABA ester (2-ethylhexyl), rarely used for the same PABA-allergy reason (slide 63; T@41924).
items.note: Slide 63 draws the ring substituent as NH2 (2-ethylhexyl 4-aminobenzoate); padimate O is the N,N-dimethylamino ester, which is what this SMILES gives. He did not discuss the amine substitution. Check before shipping.

items.name: Homosalate
items.tell: A salicylate ester (3,3,5-trimethylcyclohexyl); esters hydrolyse in skin to salicylic acid, which provides analgesia (slide 64; T@42551).

items.name: Octisalate
items.tell: A salicylate ester (2-ethylhexyl); said to be photostable, though he called that a question mark (slide 64; T@42658).
items.note: Slide 64 draws the alcohol part with O on the branch carbon (heptan-3-yl salicylate, C14H20O3); octisalate is 2-ethylhexyl salicylate (C15H22O3), which is what this SMILES gives. He taught only the salicylate part. Check before shipping.

items.name: Ensulizole
items.tell: A 2-phenylbenzimidazole carrying a sulfonic acid, which makes it water soluble (log P 1); photodegradation t1/2 about 12 h, but it must be reapplied after swimming (slide 64; T@43290).

items.name: Oxybenzone (benzophenone-3)
items.tell: A benzophenone (two benzene rings on one ketone) with 2-OH and 4-OCH3; log P about 4, highly absorbed through skin, which is a worry (slide 65; T@43624).

items.name: Octocrylene
items.tell: A cinnamate-type ester: a diphenyl-substituted C=C carrying a nitrile and a 2-ethylhexyl ester; lipophilic, the most photostable (t1/2 about 90 h), and added to stabilize others such as oxybenzone (slide 65; T@44090).
items.eg: He struck "Hydrophilic" from the slide 65 ADMET line: these esters are lipophilic and hydrolyse to inactive acids eliminated in urine (T@44969).

items.name: Bemotrizinol (BEMT)
items.tell: A 1,3,5-triazine carrying a methoxyphenyl and two 2-hydroxy-4-(2-ethylhexyloxy)phenyl rings; photostable (t1/2 4-8 h) with low skin absorption because of its high molecular weight (slide 66; T@45640).
items.eg: Slide 66 gives MW 627.81 (RDKit average MW 627.83 for C38H49N3O5).

boards.title: Depigmenting and anti-aging agents
boards.intro: For wrinkles and age spots he covered hydroquinone, alpha-hydroxy acids, hyaluronic acid and topical retinoids (tretinoin, isotretinoin and tazarotene: see the retinoid board) (slides 67-70; T@45749).

items.name: Hydroquinone
items.tell: A benzene ring with two para OH groups; it inhibits melanin biosynthesis (tyrosinase), and must be kept in an amber bottle away from light and air (slide 67; T@45980).

items.name: Benzoquinone
items.tell: The oxidation product of hydroquinone: both OH groups become C=O and the ring is no longer aromatic; coloured and inactive (slide 67; T@46104).

items.name: Lactic acid
items.tell: An alpha-hydroxy acid (OH on the carbon next to COOH, plus a methyl) found in milk; AHAs remove dead skin cells and stimulate collagen production (slide 68; T@46989).
items.eg: Slide 68 also draws glycolic (sugar cane/beet), tartaric (grapes) and malic acid (apples/grapes); see the keratolytics board for the first two.

items.name: Malic acid
items.tell: A diacid with one OH, on the carbon next to one of the carboxylic acids, so it is an alpha-hydroxy acid (slide 68; T@46330).

items.name: Hyaluronic acid (repeating unit)
items.note: Slide 69 draws the unit in brackets with open bonds at GlcA C4-O and GlcNAc C1; the generator cannot draw open bonds, so the ends are capped as OH (GlcA 4-OH, GlcNAc 1-OH, beta). Linkage GlcA beta(1-3) GlcNAc, both D.
items.tell: The repeating disaccharide of a polysaccharide (drawn here as one free unit): glucuronic acid linked to N-acetylglucosamine; endogenous, non-antigenic, and forms a hygroscopic film that holds skin moisture (slide 69; T@47478).
items.eg: High-MW HA stays on the skin surface; low-MW HA penetrates deeper (slide 69; T@47917).

boards.title: Structural features he named (11/04)
boards.intro: Features he asked the class to recognize from a drawing on 11/04 (slides 43-55; T@36832).

items.name: alpha-Hydroxy acid (SAR; R = CH3 shown)
items.tell: SAR: a COOH group, an OH on the alpha carbon (the carbon next to CO2H), and R mostly alkyl; here R is a methyl (slide 44; T@22834).

items.name: beta-Hydroxy acid (salicylic acid)
items.tell: Remove one carbon from the alpha position and the OH lands on the beta carbon, two carbons from the carboxylic acid: a beta-hydroxy acid (slide 43; T@22212).

sections.label: Four fused rings: linear vs stacked

items.name: Tetracycline nucleus: four rings in a line
items.tell: Tetracyclines have four six-membered rings fused in one straight line (1-2-3-4) (slide 55; T@35220).

items.name: Steroid nucleus: rings A-B-C-D stacked
items.tell: Steroids stack three six-membered rings and one five-membered ring (A, B, C, D) in a bent arrangement, unlike the straight line of a tetracycline; shown on ethinyl estradiol (slide 52; T@35303).

items.name: Ethyl ester prodrug (etretinate)
items.tell: An ethyl ester at the chain end needs carboxylesterase (CE) bioactivation to the free acid; etretinate to acitretin, tazarotene to tazarotenic acid (slides 50-51; T@7082).

items.name: Exposed carboxylic acid (adapalene)
items.tell: Retinoids with an exposed carboxylic acid (adapalene, trifarotene, tretinoin, acitretin) are directly active (slide 51; T@30193).

items.name: Peroxide (benzoyl peroxide)
items.tell: The O-O bond puts benzoyl peroxide in the peroxide chemical class; breaking it gives benzoic acid and a radical (slide 47; T@26051).

items.name: Macrolide (erythromycin)
items.tell: A macrolide is a large-ring lactone (cyclic ester); erythromycin is a cyclic antibiotic, azelaic acid a small linear one (slide 54; T@34968).
